answer: Seats can be priced in warm memory rather than tokens: each identity keeps a key-specific working set resident and must answer a random probe within seconds, while probes for every seat arrive at the same unpredictable moment. Because a swapped-out set misses the deadline, clones cannot timeshare the same gigabytes; k accounts need k times the resident memory and read bandwidth at once. A garden of virtual seats thus needs a real farm behind it, with no violet discount for co-location, and costs climb toward their zenith as seats multiply.
